factory-rebuild-plan.author: spec-author seat, brief A, session architect

purpose.is: This plan is the ordered path from the factory as it runs today to a factory that runs without any agent or human driving it.
purpose.is-not: This plan is not a design, a ticket list or a replacement for any existing record, and it holds no work that a step's own design has not yet cut.
purpose.relation-to-roadmap: This plan stands beside the binding 2026-10-12 roadmap at ~/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/plans/2026/10/20261012212500-roadmap.md, never replaces it and never edits it.

principle.name: No cog holds up the system
principle.quote: no cog should hold up the system, so we need a system, not agents or humans driving it
principle.statement: Every wait is a timeout with a fallback.
Every decision that can be a rule is code.
The owner is the only break-glass.

principle.name: Build mode, the factory's governance never applies to the rebuild
principle.quote: The factory's own governance never applies to the rebuild.
principle.statement: Old hooks, gates, guards, leases, watches and status rules are off for rebuild tickets.
Each new node ships dark and goes live by its own ticket with a named proof.
A rule that blocks a rebuild ticket is a defect in the rule, so the ticket proceeds and the rule gets a fix ticket.
The ledger records which rule bit.

principle.name: Shelf first
principle.quote: these are just ideas and inspiration, take it for face value, if we have better stuff from the internet, by all means we're taking that and not re-inventing the wheel, i need shit that works
principle.statement: The owner's prior work is inspiration only, and proven open source wins over anything rewritten.
Own code is reserved for glue, the LLM seat contract and the owner surface.

principle.name: Design first
principle.quote: Write the design document first and get it read before any build ticket is cut.
principle.statement: Tickets are cut from DAG nodes only.
Every node carries an XML spec under 1000 lines, a JSON schema, a checklist, agent permissions, monitoring and a runbook.

principle.name: Crew continuity
principle.quote: The same lead and investigators carry from investigation through build.
principle.statement: Context gathered in the investigation is carried forward by the same crew, so the build does not relearn it.
Under the ruling that a script drives the investigation, the continuity is the investigation files, which every later seat reads first.

principle.name: North star
principle.quote: Caves of Qud work resumes only after the factory runs as the owner intends.
principle.statement: Step R-10 is the last step, and the Caves of Qud work resumes after it and not before.

ruling.quote: One Opus lead with up to 20 Sonnet investigators is approved.
ruling.effect: The investigation runs at most 20 Sonnet investigators, one per area.

ruling.quote: The plan is XML, not markdown.
ruling.effect: This file is the plan, its XSD is the contract and markdown views are generated, never hand-edited.

ruling.quote: The plan stands beside the roadmap.
ruling.effect: The 2026-10-12 roadmap stays binding and untouched, and this plan neither edits nor replaces it.

ruling.quote: we need it driven by system, not agent
ruling.effect: A deterministic workflow script drives the investigation in place of an Opus lead, and one Opus seat does only the merge at the end.

code.name: Not started
code.meaning: The step's input record does not exist yet, or an earlier exit proof is not in the ledger.
code.acts: The system starts the step when the ordering rule is met, and no agent or human does.

code.name: Running
code.meaning: The step has a started row in the ledger and its time bound has not passed.
code.acts: The step's own script and seats act, and the system watches the time bound.

code.name: Blocked
code.meaning: The step stopped after three retries or at a gate, and always carries a reason.
code.acts: The system posts exactly one card to the owner with the reason, and the owner acts.

code.name: Done
code.meaning: Every checklist box is ticked with its proof and the exit proof is in the ledger.
code.acts: The system starts the next step, and no one else acts.

code.name: Superseded
code.meaning: The owner replaced the step, and the ledger row names what replaced it.
code.acts: Only the owner sets this status.

step.name: Investigation
step.owner-role: Workflow script, 20 Sonnet investigators, one Opus merge seat at the end
step.input: Brief B at ~/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/rebuild/2026/10/briefs/20261014-brief-B-investigation.md and the owner signal GOTEAM of 2026-10-14.
step.output: A merged inventory, root cause list, mapping, decisions-needed, unlanded and forgeo files, put in front of the owner.

exit-proof.artifact: The six lead deliverables written by the Opus merge seat after all twenty area files exist.

item.check: All twenty area files exist, one per area L01 to L13, S01 to S04 and I01 to I03.
item.evidence: An ls of the investigation directory listing twenty area files, saved in the script log.

item.check: Every area file has every heading of the findings template.
item.evidence: The per-area critic result recorded by the script, with any rerun noted.

item.check: The Opus merge seat wrote the six lead deliverables, each opening with a contents list.
item.evidence: The six file paths listed in the exit proof, each non-empty.

item.check: The completeness critic passed over the six deliverables.
item.evidence: The critic result recorded by the script.

item.check: The inventory is in front of the owner.
item.evidence: A ledger row with status question whose ref is the path of 00-INVENTORY.md.

budget.note: Twenty Sonnet investigators run under the script, and one Opus seat does only the merge at the end, with no lead agent assigning work.

failure.case: An area with no file at the time bound is rerun by a fresh Sonnet investigator, up to three times, then the step is blocked.
The script resumes from the area files already on disk and reruns only the missing ones.
An area file that fails the critic is rerun once by a fresh investigator with the critic's gaps attached.

step.name: Close lens
step.owner-role: Owner and architect, one inventory row at a time
step.input: The R-01 ledger row of status question that puts the inventory in front of the owner.
step.output: A decision record per inventory row, including the control plane shape as the first record.

exit-proof.artifact: A decision index listing every inventory row with the path of its decision record.

item.check: Every row of 00-INVENTORY.md has a decision record.
item.evidence: The index row count equals the inventory row count.

item.check: The first record is the control plane shape.
item.evidence: The first index entry names the control plane decision with the owner's chosen option.

item.check: The owner signed the close.
item.evidence: A ledger row of status complete for R-02 whose ref is the index path.

budget.note: At the time bound the step becomes blocked with one card to the owner, and nothing proceeds on a guess.

failure.case: No owner answer at the time bound blocks the step with one card, and the card is not repeated.
A row without a record leaves the index short, and the check reopens that row only.

step.name: Design
step.owner-role: Spec-author seat writes the design, a separate review seat runs the no-cog test
step.input: The R-02 decision index and the owner's close of the lens.
step.output: The DAG in Mermaid and the per-node XML specs, JSON schemas, checklists, permissions, monitoring and runbooks, merged to main and read by the owner.

exit-proof.artifact: The design merged to main, with the no-cog review result for every node.

item.check: The DAG is drawn in Mermaid and every node declares an input record and an output record.
item.evidence: The Mermaid block in rebuild/design/dag.md, rendered and checked for cycles.

item.check: Every node has an XML spec under 1000 lines, a JSON schema, a checklist, agent permissions, monitoring and a runbook.
item.evidence: A file listing per node under rebuild/design/nodes/ with line counts.

item.check: The review seat ran the no-cog test on every node and every wait has a timeout and a fallback.
item.evidence: The R-03-no-cog-review.md file with one verdict per node.

item.check: The design is merged to main and read by the owner.
item.evidence: The merged pull request URL as the ref of a ledger row, then the owner's complete row.

budget.note: One spec-author seat per node group and one review seat, all Sonnet, each living only between its input and its output.

failure.case: A node group with no spec at the time bound goes to a fresh spec-author seat, up to three times, then blocks.
A node that fails the no-cog test goes back to a fresh seat with the review verdict attached.

step.name: Land main
step.owner-role: Landing seats, one per branch group, working from the R-02 decisions
step.input: The R-03 complete row and 04-UNLANDED.md with the owner's decisions on each entry.
step.output: Every branch and pull request, including PR 35, landed, superseded or closed with a reason, so no branch holds unmerged value.

exit-proof.artifact: A disposition table with one row per branch and pull request, and the unmerged-branch listing taken after.

item.check: Every entry of 04-UNLANDED.md has a disposition of land, supersede or close with a reason.
item.evidence: The disposition table row count equals the 04-UNLANDED.md entry count.

item.check: PR 35 is landed, superseded or closed with a reason.
item.evidence: The PR 35 row in the disposition table and the pull request state from gh.

item.check: No remote branch holds unmerged value.
item.evidence: The output of git branch -r --no-merged origin/main, where every listed branch has a close reason in the table.

budget.note: Branch groups are landed in parallel only when their files do not overlap.

failure.case: A branch group with no disposition at the time bound goes to a fresh landing seat, up to three times, then blocks.
A landing whose main check fails is retried by a fresh seat with the failing output attached.
An old rule that blocks a landing is handled by the build-mode principle and the ledger records which rule bit.

step.name: Control plane
step.owner-role: Build seats cutting from design nodes, the control plane itself runs as code
step.input: The R-04 complete row and the control plane nodes of the merged design.
step.output: The first epic is built and live, and a ticket moves from cut to merged with no agent and no human driving it.

exit-proof.artifact: A run record of one ticket from cut to merged, with a timestamped log that shows no agent or human action between the two.

item.check: Each control plane node shipped dark and went live by its own ticket with a named proof.
item.evidence: One merged pull request URL per node in the run record.

item.check: One ticket moved from cut to merged with no agent and no human driving it.
item.evidence: The timestamped control plane log in R-05-run.md showing system actors only.

item.check: Every wait in the control plane has a timeout and a fallback.
item.evidence: The no-cog test output for the live nodes, saved beside the run record.

budget.note: Tickets are small, one concern each, and are built by ephemeral seats that leave after posting their result.

failure.case: A ticket with no progress at its time bound is retried by a fresh seat, up to three times, then the step blocks.
The control plane resumes from the ledger and the state store, which are the only state.
A node whose proof fails is retried by a fresh seat with the failing output attached.
An old rule that blocks a ticket does not stop it, the rule gets a fix ticket and the ledger records which rule bit.

step.name: Seats as ephemeral workers
step.owner-role: Build seats, with the seat contract written as glue code
step.input: The R-05 complete row and the seat nodes of the merged design.
step.output: A seat spawns from a ticket, posts its result and is gone, with bring-up under a measured bound stated in the design.

exit-proof.artifact: A seat lifecycle record with the measured bring-up time beside the bound stated in the design.

item.check: A seat spawned from a ticket posted its result and exited without an owner or architect action.
item.evidence: The spawn, result and exit timestamps in R-06-seat-lifecycle.md.

item.check: Bring-up time is measured and sits under the bound stated in the design.
item.evidence: Ten measured bring-ups and the design bound, recorded side by side.

item.check: A follow-up such as a failed test brings up a fresh seat and never reuses the finished one.
item.evidence: A recorded failure case where the retry seat has a new id.

budget.note: Seats are cogs, and none is a gate.

failure.case: A bring-up over its bound is killed and retried by a fresh seat, up to three times, then the step blocks.
A seat result that fails its proof check goes to a fresh seat with the failure attached.

step.name: herdr demoted to a window
step.owner-role: Build seats removing every scheduling and storage use of herdr
step.input: The R-06 complete row and the herdr demotion node of the merged design.
step.output: herdr schedules nothing and stores nothing, and the line runs with it closed.

exit-proof.artifact: A run record of tickets merged while herdr was stopped, with a scan showing no herdr scheduling or storage use.

item.check: No line component calls herdr to schedule, route or store anything.
item.evidence: A grep of the control plane code for herdr calls, with its output saved in the record.

item.check: The line ran with herdr closed.
item.evidence: At least one ticket merged between a herdr stop and a herdr start, with timestamps.

budget.note: herdr stays available as a window for the owner to watch, and nothing depends on it.

failure.case: A removal ticket with no progress at its bound goes to a fresh seat, up to three times, then blocks.
A line run that stalls with herdr closed fails the proof, and a fresh seat retries with the stall record attached.

step.name: Single state store and owner surface
step.owner-role: Build seats moving state into one store and pointing bearings at it
step.input: The R-07 complete row and the state store and owner surface nodes of the merged design.
step.output: Bearings reads one store, and no event file is written inside the repository.

exit-proof.artifact: A record of bearings reading the single store and a repository check after a run that finds no event file inside the repository.

item.check: Bearings reads exactly one store.
item.evidence: The bearings read trace listing a single store path.

item.check: No event file is written inside the repository by a run.
item.evidence: The output of git status --porcelain after a run, with no event path in it.

item.check: The old stores are retired with a documented cleanup command.
item.evidence: The cleanup command in the README and its dry-run output.

budget.note: The owner monitoring surface stays available throughout, and a halt never stops it.

failure.case: A migration ticket with no progress at its bound goes to a fresh seat, up to three times, then blocks.
A repository check that finds an event file fails the proof and goes to a fresh seat with the path attached.
An old hook that blocks a migration ticket does not stop it, and the ledger records which hook bit.

step.name: Line proves itself
step.owner-role: The line itself, with seats only as the workers of the tickets it runs
step.output: Ten consecutive tickets merged without a stall.

exit-proof.artifact: A table of ten consecutive tickets from cut to merged with timestamps and no stall record between them.

item.check: Ten tickets merged in a row, each moving from cut to merged on the line alone.
item.evidence: Ten merged pull request URLs in the table, in order.

item.check: No ticket in the run stalled past its time bound.
item.evidence: The stall record count for the run, which is zero.

budget.note: A stall resets the count to zero, and the step is blocked after three resets.

failure.case: A stalled ticket resets the consecutive count, its cause becomes a fix ticket, and the run restarts, up to three times.
A merged ticket whose proof fails afterward resets the count and goes to a fresh seat with the failure attached.

step.name: Bootstrap
step.owner-role: The same line, run against a second repository
step.input: The R-09 complete row and the owner's choice of the second repository.
step.output: A ticket in another repository merged by the same line, after which Caves of Qud work resumes.

exit-proof.artifact: The merged pull request URL in the other repository with the line's run log for that ticket.

item.check: The ticket was cut, run and merged by the same line with no change to the line for the new repository.
item.evidence: The merged pull request URL and a diff of line configuration showing only the repository entry.

item.check: Caves of Qud work is released to resume.
item.evidence: A ledger row of status complete for R-10 that names the release.

budget.note: Only a repository entry may differ between the first repository and the second.

failure.case: A ticket with no progress at its bound is retried by a fresh seat, up to three times, then the step blocks.
A merge that fails its proof goes to a fresh seat with the failure attached, and the line is not edited for one repository.

ordering-rule.s: No later step starts before the earlier step's exit proof is in the ledger.
The ledger is the only record that a step is done, and a file on disk without a ledger row proves nothing.

case.meaning: No progress is made past the step's time bound.
case.detection: The system compares the last ledger row time and the output files with the time bound every minute.
case.recovery: The system ends the stalled work and starts a fresh seat or script run with the stall record attached.
case.acts: The system acts and no agent or human does.

case.meaning: The script, a seat, a pane or the session dies.
case.detection: The system finds a started ledger row with no live worker and no exit proof.
case.recovery: The work resumes from the ledger, which is the only state, and reruns only what the exit proof lacks.
case.acts: The system acts, and a cold session resumes by the recovery section if the system itself is down.

case.meaning: The exit proof fails its check.
case.detection: The step's check runs on the exit proof and returns a failure.
case.recovery: A fresh seat retries with the failure attached, and never the seat that failed.
case.acts: The system spawns the fresh seat and no agent or human does.

case.meaning: An old hook, gate, guard, lease, watch or status rule blocks a rebuild ticket.
case.detection: The ticket's seat or the system reports a refusal that names the old rule.
case.recovery: The build-mode principle applies, so the ticket proceeds, the rule gets a fix ticket and the ledger row records which rule bit.
case.acts: The system proceeds and cuts the fix ticket, and the owner is told only through the ledger.

recovery.read-first: A cold session needs nothing but this XML, the ledger and main, and it reads them in the order below.
recovery.file: The plan on main, which names every step, proof and rule.
The contract the plan is validated against.
The only record of what is started, done or blocked.
The exit proofs written so far.
Where every output lives and the cleanup command.
recovery.rebuild-command: Run rebuild/bin/plan-validate.sh, then rebuild/bin/plan-to-rail.sh, then rebuild/rail.sh from a fresh worktree of main, and publish the built page to the URL in the latest checkpoint row.
recovery.action: Create a fresh worktree from origin/main and run the plan-validate.sh script, and stop if it fails.
Show the ledger with the ledger.sh --show option and find the first step with no complete row, which is the current step.
If the current step has a started row, check whether its exit proof paths exist and pass the step checklist.
If the proof exists and passes, append a complete row, otherwise start a fresh seat or script run with the failure attached.
If the last row for the step is blocked, read its ref and do nothing more, because the owner has one card waiting.
After every ledger row, rebuild the page with rail.sh and republish it to the same URL with the Artifact tool.
After the first publish, append a checkpoint row whose ref is the artifact URL, so a cold session republishes to the same URL.

change-rule.s: Only the owner adds or removes steps.
Agents append ledger rows and nothing else.
The status in this file is the status at issue, and the ledger is the live state.

ledger.usage: RIME_LEDGER=ledger-path RIME_SEAT=seat-name ~/.claude/skills/execution-rail/bin/ledger.sh step status "text of fifteen words or fewer" [ref]
ledger.columns: The columns are at_utc, step, status, text, by and ref, and the status is started, complete, blocked, issue, question or checkpoint.
ledger.first-row: R-01 started: Investigation launched: script-driven, 20 Sonnet investigators, three tracks.
